core.title: Assert telemetry tests on a captured sink, not on a return value
core.given: A telemetry test: a test file identified as telemetry by the profile's markers — a telemetry-test identification header, a telemetry URN kind segment, or a telemetry-test file-name pattern (any one of them)
core.when: the test is written or changed
core.then: The test asserts on the emission itself via the captured sink, using the profile's emission-assertion constructs.
prefer: Capture the emitter (spy, mock, or captured array the emitter writes to — the thing whose content is the emission), inject it into the unit under test, and assert on it.
Assert the exact event identity and payload on the sink, joining the captured-sink and exact-identity requirements.
avoid: Asserting only on the unit under test's return value — a return value is not a sink; it proves the unit ran, not that the item fired.
Satisfying the check with an emission-vocabulary assertion that does not inspect what the sink actually received.
unless: The test is not telemetry-identified; only telemetry-identified tests are scanned, and the profile's general test rule governs the rest.
The rule family has not been adopted in the repository (inert until adoption, like every rule in this family).
core.why: Dashboards, alerts and downstream analytics are built on the emission; a return-value check proves the unit ran, not that the event fired — only the sink saw it fire.
evidence: The telemetry test contains an assertion from the profile's emission-assertion vocabulary on the captured sink.
The stack's telemetry-test check reports no finding for the file.
verification: Scope: only telemetry-identified tests are scanned; identification is the OR of the profile's markers — the telemetry-test identification header, the telemetry URN kind segments, and the telemetry-test file-name pattern — and non-identified tests are out of scope (the profile's general test rule governs them).
Scan scope is the profile's test languages: the check applies only to test files written in those languages; files in other languages are out of scope.
The predicate is deliberately the emission-assertion vocabulary from the profile, not a data-flow analysis: it names what a test must contain, not what the runtime did.
Term captured_sink: the spy, mock or captured array the emitter writes to — the thing whose CONTENT is the emission. A return value is not a sink.
The rule is inert until the repository adopts the family.
Severity 3; disposition strict: every finding fails the check — no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

fires: Writing or editing a telemetry-identified test whose assertions only check the unit under test's return value.
A telemetry-identified test file that never asserts on the captured sink (the emitter's spy, mock or captured array).
doesNotFire: A test file that is not telemetry-identified — the profile's general test rule governs it.
Repositories that have not adopted this rule family (inert until adoption).
A telemetry test that already asserts on the captured sink with one of the profile's emission-assertion constructs.

Bun's generic 'test' file kind is unrestricted: every test kind can be a telemetry test. Neutralized to ALL test roles in the vocabulary — unit_test, acceptance_test and e2e_test — so no telemetry-identified test kind (end-to-end included) falls out of activation.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (assert on the emission via the captured sink, not the return value) is fully stack-neutral and is carried whole, with both exceptions intact. Telemetry-test identification stays an OR of three alternatives, each supplied by its documented vocabulary key: the identification header (urn.header#telemetry_test), the telemetry URN kind segments (urn.test_kinds#telemetry), and the colocation file-name pattern (suffix.telemetry_test). The emission-assertion matcher vocabulary has no dedicated key and fits idiom.test_constructs (assertions and matchers), so it is the map entry idiom.test_constructs#emission_assertion; no new keys are proposed. The check's language scope is the map entry tooling.language_scopes#test_languages, keeping tooling.languages reserved for production-source languages per its documented meaning. Bun's generic 'test' file kind maps to every test role in the vocabulary — unit_test, acceptance_test and e2e_test — so telemetry-identified tests of any kind stay in activation; the core's activation is neither narrower nor broader than Bun's. The exact-identity-and-payload assertion stays in prefer only: an existing sink assertion exempts the test (doesNotFire) without any identity/payload qualification. Remaining Bun-only content: the fix_hint code snippet with its project-specific event URN, the validator id bun_telemetry_test, and the exact finding id telemetry_test_identified_by_header_or_urn — none has a neutral equivalent, and the core's verification describes the check generically. The severity number 3 belongs to the source's severity scale and is kept in core verification only because severity/disposition are specified to live there; a foreign stack instantiating this core may use its own scale position for 'not advisory'. Note the predicate stays vocabulary-based by design (no data-flow analysis), so a superficially sink-shaped assertion can still game it — that residual weakness is exactly what avoid[1] guards, and it is inherited, not introduced.
